chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Wefland, the hard-drinking drummer of the Detroit Symphony
summary: A brilliant but alcoholic drummer and xylophonist who played with the Detroit Symphony, whom Norvo sobered up for Saturday concerts at a speakeasy near the Fox.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: No. I tell you what happened after that. I had a drummer friend I knew. And I met him -- I'd met him once in Minneapolis when I played a theater there. I was playing xylophone -- he was a xylophone player and he played for the symphony. And I'd met him there, the -- he was at

-- quite a drunk and tremendous talent. So, he was playing with the Detroit Symphony, I used to get him out -- get him ready for the Saturday concert, I'd go -- from Eight Mile Road where from the University, I'd go in town, he lived at the Berkshire, I used to try and get him up, get him sobered up, and to make the Saturday afternoon concert. So I'd take him over to a speakeasy by the Fox Theater, stagedoor, right across the street there was a house with a speakeasy. I'd take him in there. And he'd have a whiskey sour, it wouldn't stay down, he'd have maybe four or five and they wouldn't stay down, finally he'd get and they'd have about five or six lined up. So he'd take the one and it'd stay down and he'd drink the other five real quick. And he'd -- funny thing, he had a disease where half of his face was paralyzed, so when he laughed, just one side would laugh, see.

And he would say, he'd look at me, and he'd straighten out in a few minutes, he'd look at his hands and they'd be shaking like this, he'd take his hands like -- "I'm going to have a helluva roll today --
Oh, Wellin, he was something else -- he was a wonderful man.
And -- he'd finally lost the job there, but during that speakeasy, I was there and I'll tell you that
was a good band the Fox, had, Raphael Mendez, was in that, you know the trumpet player?
